events.credibility_reason: The suggestion that the tetrahedron packs worse than the ball was overtaken by explicit tetrahedron packings of density about 0.856; the paper itself was not opened.
The Ulam verification is attributed to this paper only by one citing paper; the paper's own abstract concerns non-convex particles.

why: The statement asks which convex solid minimises the optimal packing density, which is a universal claim (the ball) over all 3D convex solids. Numerical dense packings of specific solids (Platonic, tetrahedron dimer, Johnson/Catalan checks) each show one or finitely many solids beating the ball, so they are instances. The Conway–Torquato suggestion settles nothing. The close call is Kallus 2012 (and 2013): the competing reading treats it as partial progress. I scored it variant because it proves a local inequality for lattice density phi, not for the general packing density delta the conjecture concerns, and only for origin-symmetric bodies. Proving something about a different quantity changes the question rather than restricting it. A local theorem about delta itself would have been a case. All post-snapshot items concern the planar Reinhardt analogue, high-dimensional sphere packing, covering, or packing minima, so they are variants; the OpenAI announcement does not touch the problem, so it is none. No AI system contributed mathematics to any event.
doubts: Kallus 2012 could be read as a case (a local restriction) rather than a variant. It is scored variant because phi is lattice density rather than delta; if lattice density were taken to be the question's quantity, it would be a pre-snapshot case, which still leaves the problem open. The journal publications are taken as digestion of the published arguments. They are not verification of the numerical optima.
